thread:
violet (new-dev): Hi all — trying PHP quickstart inside our corp network. First call returns 403 and body: `workspace_limited`. I set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env.

rahul (devex): Welcome! Quick question: are you behind a proxy that rewrites headers? We've seen `Authorization` or `X-Api-Key` stripped by some gateways.

violet (new-dev): Could be. The app runs in an internal container and the org proxy adds hop. How should I debug?

tess (sdk-php): If you run `curl -v` against the API from the container you should see the outbound request headers. Our PHP client sends `Authorization: Bearer $KEY`. Some proxies drop `Authorization`. We also log a small diagnostic when the server responds 403 but missing the structured key.

violet (new-dev): Ran `docker exec` and did `curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/ping -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\"` and the outgoing shows the header present. But server still returns workspace_limited.

proxy-bot: Auto: Proxy gateway rewrite rule matched pattern `strip-sensitive-headers` on egress path for service `redwood-api`.

rahul (devex): Aha. Proxy bot confirms header stripping. In our docs we recommend exposing the key as `X-Redwood-Api-Key` as a fallback when Authorization is blocked. The SDKs also support `REDWOOD_API_KEY` env var -> header mapping.

violet (new-dev): Ok. I tried adding `-H \"X-Redwood-Api-Key: $KEY\"` to the curl call and it succeeds locally, but the quickstart app still 403s. The quickstart uses Guzzle and ends up sending only Authorization.

tess (sdk-php): Two options: (1) update the quickstart entrypoint to set env var `REDWOOD_API_KEY` so the client adds fallback header, or (2) change the proxy rule to allow `Authorization` through for your dev subnet. Also check workspace billing; sometimes limited workspaces return same 403 shape which confuses debugging.

maya (billing-cs): I checked your org (violet-corp-dev). Billing status: "Limited: payment method required". That would also produce `workspace_limited` semantics for write endpoints. If you want a quick dev unlock I can enable sandbox access for 24h.

violet (new-dev): Wait, that's surprising — I did the signup flow and thought we were on trial. The UI had an SSO redirect when I clicked "Add billing" and I closed it so maybe it never finished.

rahul (devex): Common pattern: corporate SSO redirects can leave the billing page incomplete. Two parallel things to try: finish billing flow or request dev unlock. For header stripping, we should surface a clearer message in quickstarts when both header and billing checks fail.

tess (sdk-php): I'll patch the PHP quickstart to: - attempt `X-Redwood-Api-Key` if `Authorization` appears absent at the server, - print a clear diagnostic if server returns workspace_limited with a link to billing docs. Opening PR SDK-PHP-198.

onboard-bot: Auto: Created ticket BILL-5077 for payments team; assigned to maya.

maya (billing-cs): Enabled a 24h dev unlock for your org. Also sent a DM with the billing completion link.

violet (new-dev): Thanks — after adding the fallback env and with unlock, first call works. I'll open a small README PR describing corp proxy gotchas and the SSO/billing trap.

rahul (devex): Great. Follow-ups: update examples/php README, add a short runtime check that prints \"Authorization header may be stripped by proxies — try X-Redwood-Api-Key or export REDWOOD_API_KEY\" and link to billing troubleshooting.

violet (new-dev): Will do. Logging this thread so others behind corp proxies don't waste time. :+1:
